title: Scenario 1: Quality vs Compatibility
purpose: Test whether a small compatibility advantage (0.96 vs 0.94) competes with a substantial feedback-quality difference (3.2 vs 4.8 stars with 30 reviews).

candidates.name: Tutor B (Slightly Higher Compatibility, Lower Rating)

title: Scenario 2: Cold Start vs Established Tutor
purpose: Test whether a single 5.0 rating (n=1) is appropriately shrunk toward the prior rather than overpowering established 4.7 evidence (n=40).

title: Scenario 3: New Tutor With No Reviews
purpose: Test cold-start behavior when no feedback exists. The new tutor must receive neutral prior treatment and not suffer an unfair penalty.

title: Scenario 4: Strong Compatibility vs Strong Feedback
purpose: Test whether feedback can overwhelm a large compatibility advantage (0.98 vs 0.88) when feedback weight increases from moderate to aggressive levels.

title: Scenario 5: Similar Compatibility, Different Feedback
purpose: Test whether feedback meaningfully distinguishes candidates when recommendation compatibility is nearly identical (0.91 vs 0.90).

title: Scenario 6: Same Rating, Different Evidence Strength
purpose: Demonstrate Bayesian shrinkage and evidence confidence when empirical ratings are identical (5.0 stars) but review counts differ vastly (n=1 vs n=40).
